skill.name: azure-mgmt-fabric-py
skill.description: Use the Azure Fabric Management SDK for Python to manage Microsoft Fabric capacities and resource lifecycle tasks.
skill.summary: Manage Microsoft Fabric capacities with focused Python Azure SDK examples.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static external-command matches are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline code, not executable Ruby or shell backticks. The environment variable reads are standard Azure SDK configuration. A medium contextual risk remains because the skill guides mutating Fabric capacity operations that can affect billing and resources.

remediation.issue: Mutating Azure capacity operations can change billing or remove resources.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and a preview of target subscription, resource group, capacity name, SKU, and action before create, update, suspend, resume, or delete calls.

remediation.issue: Dependency installation examples use unpinned package names.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend trusted package sources and version ranges for azure-mgmt-fabric and azure-identity when users need reproducible environments.

remediation.issue: Environment examples assume local Azure context is correct.
remediation.suggestion: Add validation steps for subscription ID, resource group, tenant, and least-privilege role assignments before running examples.

semantic_findings.title: Cloud Resource Mutation Requires Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The skill teaches create, update, suspend, resume, and delete operations for Microsoft Fabric capacities. These actions can change billing or remove cloud resources if an agent runs them without explicit approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples call Azure management methods that create, scale, and delete Fabric capacities. The behavior matches the skill scope, but it creates operational and billing risk if automated without confirmation.

content.value_statement: Microsoft Fabric capacity management requires Azure SDK setup and careful long-running operation handling. This skill gives focused examples for creating, scaling, pausing, and deleting capacities.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation commands for azure-mgmt-fabric and azure-identity.
Initializes FabricMgmtClient with DefaultAzureCredential and a subscription ID.
Demonstrates capacity create, get, list, update, suspend, resume, and delete flows.
Lists Fabric capacity SKUs and capacity states.
Explains long-running operation handling with result waits and polling.
limitations: Does not validate Azure permissions or tenant policy.
Does not include production retry, logging, or error handling patterns.
Examples can change billable Azure resources when run.
Requires existing Azure credentials and subscription context.

use_cases.title: Create a Test Capacity
use_cases.description: Set up a small Microsoft Fabric capacity with Python SDK examples and required Azure inputs.

use_cases.title: Control Capacity Cost
use_cases.description: Suspend and resume Fabric capacities around workload schedules after confirming business impact.

use_cases.title: Review Capacity Inventory
use_cases.description: List capacities, inspect states, and compare available SKUs in a resource group or subscription.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Fabric SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to install the Python packages and configure environment variables for Microsoft Fabric capacity management.

prompt_templates.title: Read Capacity Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me retrieve one Fabric capacity and explain which inputs I must provide before running the script.

prompt_templates.title: Manage Capacity Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a step-by-step workflow to create, scale, suspend, resume, and delete a Fabric capacity with confirmation gates.

prompt_templates.title: Design Guarded Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe automation plan for Fabric capacities that handles long-running operations, cost controls, tags, and rollback checks.

output_examples.input: I need to create a small Fabric capacity for a test workspace.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify required Azure inputs, select an F2 SKU, and describe the create operation with a confirmation step.

output_examples.input: How can I reduce Fabric cost overnight?
output: Review active capacities by resource group.
Suspend unused capacity after confirming business impact.

output_examples.input: I need to scale a capacity from F2 to F4.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline an update operation, warn about cost changes, and include long-running operation handling.

best_practices: Require explicit approval before create, update, suspend, resume, or delete operations.
Use least-privilege Azure roles for service principals or developer credentials.
Tag capacities for owner, environment, and cost center before production use.
anti_patterns: Running destructive examples against production subscriptions without confirmation.
Hardcoding tenant, subscription, resource group, or user values in shared scripts.
Ignoring long-running operation status after starting a capacity change.

faq.question: Does this skill create Fabric resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and workflow guidance. Any execution depends on the agent, user approval, and Azure credentials.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it need Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use DefaultAzureCredential and require a valid subscription context.

faq.question: Can it delete capacities?
faq.answer: Yes. The source includes delete examples, so users should require confirmation before running mutating actions.

faq.question: Does it manage Fabric workspaces?
faq.answer: No. The documented scope focuses on Fabric capacities and related management operations.

faq.question: Is it production ready?
faq.answer: It is a starting point. Add validation, policy checks, retries, and logging before production automation.
